title: Stoker metadata — runtime
description: `runtimes/<key>.json`: one runtime a machine needs before games will run — Visual C++ 2015-2022 (x64), DirectX June 2010, PhysX — identified by what it is, not by any copy of it. Everything about installing it once per machine is here, once: how to tell it is already there, how to run its installer silently, which exit codes mean success. A build names it by key; forty games that need it cost one installer run. Its copies are listed below because games bundle their own and those differ — a 2019 game ships 14.28, a 2023 one 14.36 — and the newest a machine needs is the one that runs. The installers are never in the repository: a copy is recognised by its hash in a game's files, or downloaded from its publisher.

key.description: The file's name. Stable across every version of the runtime; the architecture is part of it, because the x86 and x64 forms register separately and one does not satisfy the other.

name.description: What a person reads: "Microsoft Visual C++ 2015-2022 Redistributable (x64)".

platform.description: The one platform it installs on. A build serving several platforms keeps one dependency list, and a runtime for another platform than the one being installed is skipped.

install.description: How any copy's installer is run. On the runtime, not the copy, because the switches are a property of the runtime: supplied once, they hold for every copy a game will ever bundle.

arguments.description: The switches that make it install without a window: `/install /quiet /norestart`. Absent when nobody knows them, which leaves the runtime unable to install unattended.

successExitCodes.description: Exit codes that mean it worked. Not only zero: 1638 is "a newer version is already installed", 3010 "done, restart pending" — failing either would fail an install that worked.

requires64BitOs.description: Skip it on 32-bit Windows; every copy of an x64 runtime needs a 64-bit system.

copies.description: Known copies of the runtime's installer, newest first.

detection.description: How a machine tells the runtime is already there — and so whether a copy's installer needs to run at all.

oneOf.description: Nothing to probe: the only evidence is the launcher's own record of having installed it on this machine. Weaker than a probe, because it cannot see a copy something else installed, but never wrong.
A registry value exists, and reads at least the copy's `version` when the copy has one — which is what makes an older runtime upgrade rather than count as satisfied.

key.description: The full key, hive included: `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\VisualStudio\14.0\VC\Runtimes\x64`. Read in the registry view of the runtime's architecture.

oneOf.description: A file exists. For runtimes that write no registry marker.

path.description: An absolute path on the machine, environment variables in the platform's own form: `%SystemRoot%\System32\d3dx9_43.dll`, `$HOME/.local/lib/x.so`.

version.description: The version this copy installs, as the detection probe reads it: a machine with less installs this copy. Also how copies are ranked; absent, the copy only ever satisfies the ledger.

installer.description: The file that is run. A game's bundled copy is recognised by this file's BLAKE3 in the game's manifest (`_CommonRedist/vcredist/2019/VC_redist.x64.exe`), wherever the game put it; a download is checked against the SHA-256.

package.description: For an installer that needs files beside it (DirectX's `DXSETUP.exe` and its cabinets): the whole folder by fingerprint — without Steam's `installscript.vdf`, which names the shipping game and would make two identical copies differ — and where the installer sits in it.

steamRan.description: Where Steam records having run this copy's installer, and the value it writes there — proof of presence for a runtime with only the ledger to go on. Its absence proves nothing: it is a record of what Steam did, not a probe of the machine.
